correctness.rationale: For the published three-species recurrence with zero adult-prey carryover and negative-binomial shape-one escape, \(x_{t+1}=R_Jx_th_{t+1}\), while \(y_{t+1}=R_Ay_th_t/(1+y_t)\). Therefore \(q_t=h_ty_t/x_t\) obeys \(q_{t+1}=(R_A/R_J)q_t/(1+y_t)\). The capacity bound gives \(x_t\le R_J\) after one generation, and \(y_t=R_Jx_{t-1}q_t\). For \(R_A<R_J\), the ratio decays geometrically; at \(R_A=R_J\), either the ratio tends to zero or its positive limit forces \(\sum_t\log(1+y_t)<\infty\). Both prove adult predator extinction. For Beverton–Holt, interior fixed points force \(h=1/R_J\), \(y=R_A/R_J-1\), and \(x=rR_J/(R_A+r-1)-1\), yielding precisely the strict two-sided wedge and direct substitution. The exact-rational checker exercised 630 transitions; finite tests do not establish the all-time limit.

originality.rationale: Seno and Goyal (2026) introduce the general model and establish only equilibrium-level necessary replacement ordering (Lemma 6); their main fully inspected article neither establishes global adult-stage extinction on arbitrary positive trajectories nor derives the exact complete coexistence wedge for the shape-one negative-binomial specialization. The distinctive multiplicative q identity uses a particular escape law and is not implied by their exponential detailed model. Earlier one-parasitoid Beverton-Holt/negative-binomial analyses have fewer interacting species and are not implication-level coverage. Priority remains limited by inaccessible or unindexed older work.

value.rationale: Competition between juvenile-stage and adult-stage predators is biologically consequential, including under non-equilibrium recurrent fluctuations. The exact multiplicative ratio law gives a global exclusion decision even if the surviving community cycles. A complete nonempty, sharp two-sided equilibrium existence wedge for natural Beverton-Holt recruitment shows that both too little and too much adult predator reproduction obstruct three-species steady coexistence. These are structural properties of natural model parameters, not isolated calculations.
